title: Construction of a composite catalytic method to produce thermotropic liquid crystalline polyesters by comprehensively revisiting the acetylation and transesterification reactions separately
content: Thermotropic liquid crystalline polymers (TLCPs) are high-performance specialty materials with exceptional thermal stability, mechanical strength, and dielectric properties. However, the conventional “one-pot” melt polycondensation strategy suffers from a black-box effect, where a single catalyst is typically employed for all the involved elementary reactions, possibly limiting both efficiency and product quality. In this work, the two critical elementary reactions, acetylation of p-hydroxybenzoic acid (HBA) and transesterification of acetylated monomers, were comprehensively revisited. Acetylation at 200 °C revealed that organic catalysts, particularly 1-methylimidazole (NMI) and triphenylphosphine (PPh3), achieved superior acetylation efficiencies (≥98.8%) and suppressed oligomer formation more effectively than Lewis acid catalysts. In contrast, the transesterification of 4-acetoxybenzoic acid (ABA) and 6-acetoxy-2-naphthoic acid (ANA) was most efficiently catalyzed by zinc acetate (Zn(OAc)2), yielding TLCPs with an intrinsic viscosity (I.V.) of 5.90 dL g−1 and a single melting peak at ∼280 °C, indicating nearly thorough transesterification. Based on these findings, a novel composite catalytic method combining NMI/PPh3 and Zn(OAc)2 was developed for the “one-pot” melt polycondensation of HBA and 6-hydroxy-2-naphthoic acid (HNA). The composite catalyst delivered an acetylation efficiency of 99.5% and produced TLCPs with an I.V. of up to 6.64 dL g−1 while also yielding a lighter-colored product compared to that obtained with Zn(OAc)2 alone. This work provides a highly efficient strategy for TLCP synthesis and offers valuable novel insights for designing advanced liquid crystalline polymers to meet the rapidly evolving modern demands.
